doc_friction.issue: Step 0 sent the run to security alert #1, but the queue was built from a scan older than PR 18676 and four open PRs (18806-18809) were already handling it; the alert file had no step to check staleness or open PRs first (PR 18808 adds one).

Crashes with a CalledProcessError traceback on a shallow clone where merge-base with origin/main is unknown; needed a commit plus fetch before it would run (PR 18791 adds a stale --base warning, not this).

deviations.why: Step 0 says take the top security alert; alerts #1-#7 are triaged false positives in open PR 18809 and the queue is stale per PR 18808, so taking one would duplicate.
deviations.result: Routed to redteam; shipped two real money-affecting fixes.

real_defects.issue: isChangeOrder read items numbered CO1, C.O. 3 or C.O.3 as base-contract lines: original contract sum inflated, net change orders understated, and a deductive 'CO1' line raised a false high finding ('negative scheduled value on a base-contract line'). Repro: compute([{item:'1',scheduled:'10000',thisPeriod:'5000'},{item:'CO1',scheduled:'-1500'}]) gave original $8,500, net CO $0. Fixed regex; failing-first test.

quickbooksLines accepted a negative 'retainage held' (the guide tells people to enter retainage in QuickBooks as a negative number, so typing -4000 is natural) and turned it into a +$4,000 Retainage line: the invoice billed the retainage instead of holding it (total $44,000 instead of $36,000 on $40,000). Now refused with a message; label says 'as a positive amount'. Failing-first test.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: senior dev: mutation triage, two defect repros, tests and fixes in two products

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
